# Job Scheduler: requirements

A service that holds job configurations for several applications and runs those jobs.
The code a job runs already exists in the repo. Build it in Go with Gin + GORM on SQLite
(`github.com/glebarez/sqlite`). The skeleton is in this repo: `cmd/server/main.go` reads
`JOB_SCHEDULER_DB` and `PORT`; `internal/app/app.go` holds the settings, database and routes.

## Roles
- **Super admin** (`users.is_super_admin = true`): may do every operation in every application.
- **App admin**: a membership with role `app_admin` in an application. May do every
  operation inside that application, including managing its members.
- **Executor**: a membership with role `executor`. May view that application's job
  configs and runs, and run and cancel jobs. May not create or change configs or
  members, and may not view the member list.
- A user who is **not a member** of an application gets **404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`**
  for anything in it, as if it didn't exist.
- A member without the needed role gets **403 `{"detail": "You do not have permission
  to perform this action."}`**.

## Data model (table and column names are fixed; other code depends on them)
- `users`: `id`, `email` (unique), `hashed_password` (bcrypt), `is_super_admin`, `is_active`
- `applications`: `id`, `name` (unique, 1–100 characters)
- `memberships`: `id`, `user_id`, `application_id`, `role` (`app_admin` | `executor`).
  One membership per (user, application).
- `job_configs`: `id`, `application_id`, `name` (a label), `job_name` (the stable id),
  `version`, `code_path`, `command`, `is_cron`, `cron_expr` (nullable), `is_active`,
  `created_by`, `created_at`
- `job_runs`: `id`, `job_config_id`, `application_id`, `trigger` (`manual` | `cron`),
  `triggered_by` (nullable), `status` (`queued` | `running` | `succeeded` | `failed` |
  `cancelled`), `created_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `exit_code` (all three nullable)

## Ticket 1: users, login, applications, members
- `POST /auth/login` takes `{email, password}` and returns `{access_token, token_type: "bearer"}`
  (a JWT, HS256 with `Settings.SecretKey`; `sub` = user id; it expires after 60 minutes).
  - A wrong password or an unknown email answers 401 `{"detail": "Incorrect email or password"}`.
  - An inactive user answers 403 `{"detail": "Inactive user"}`.
- Every other route needs a bearer token:
  - no token: 401 `{"detail": "Not authenticated"}`;
  - a bad token: 401 `{"detail": "Could not validate credentials"}`;
  - an inactive user: 403 `"Inactive user"`.
- `GET /users/me` returns `{id, email, is_super_admin, is_active}`.
- `POST /users` (super admin only) creates a user from `{email, password}`. Passwords are 8 to 72 bytes
  (bcrypt's limit); anything else answers 422. It answers 201
  with the user. A duplicate email answers 409; an invalid email answers 422.
- `POST /applications` (super admin only) takes `{name}` and answers 201 `{id, name}`. A
  duplicate name answers 409; a name that is empty or over 100 characters answers 422.
- `GET /applications` returns every application to the super admin; everyone else gets
  only the ones they are a member of. Ordered by id.
- `GET /applications/{id}` returns the application.
- `GET /applications/{id}/members` (app admin or super admin) returns `[{user_id, role}]`.
- `PUT /applications/{id}/members/{user_id}` takes `{role}`. It creates the membership, or
  changes its role (never a second membership), and answers 200 `{user_id, role}`. An
  unknown user answers 404; an invalid role answers 422.
- `DELETE /applications/{id}/members/{user_id}` answers 204. If there is no such
  membership, it answers 404.
- A refused or invalid request writes nothing.

## Ticket 2: job configs
- `POST /applications/{app}/jobs` (app admin or super admin) takes `{name, job_name, version,
  code_path, command, is_cron, cron_expr}` and answers 201 with the config.
  - A new config is **inactive**, and `created_by` is the caller.
- **Validation** (each failure answers 422 and writes nothing):
  - `job_name`: `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, 1–100 characters.
  - `name`: 1–100 characters.
  - `version`: 1–50 characters.
  - `code_path`: relative, inside the repo, with no `..` and not absolute.
  - `command`: 1–1000 characters. Its executable (the first token) must be in the
    allowlist `Settings.ExecutableAllowlist` (`python`, `bash`, `sh`).
  - `is_cron` true needs a valid 5-field `cron_expr`; `is_cron` false needs `cron_expr`
    to be null.
- `(application, job_name, version)` is unique. A duplicate answers 409. The same job_name
  and version in another application is fine.
- `GET /applications/{app}/jobs` (any member) returns the configs ordered by id.
  `GET /applications/{app}/jobs/{id}` returns one config.
- `POST .../jobs/{id}/activate` (app admin or super admin) makes this version active and
  every other version of the same job inactive. **At most one active version per job.**
  `POST .../jobs/{id}/deactivate` makes it inactive.
- **A registered version never changes.** There is no edit route, so `PATCH` answers 405;
  a change means registering a new version.
- A config id from another application, under this application's path, answers 404.

## Ticket 3: runs
- `POST /applications/{app}/jobs/{id}/runs` (any member, or the super admin) answers 201
  with a run: `trigger="manual"`, `triggered_by` = the caller, `status="queued"`.
  - An inactive config answers 409 and creates no run.
  - **At most one queued or running run per config:** another one answers 409.
- `GET /applications/{app}/jobs/{id}/runs` returns the config's runs ordered by id;
  `GET /applications/{app}/runs/{run_id}` returns one run. A run has: id,
  job_config_id, application_id, trigger, triggered_by, status, created_at, started_at,
  finished_at, exit_code.
- `POST /applications/{app}/runs/{run_id}/cancel` (any member, or the super admin) moves a
  queued or running run to `cancelled` and sets `finished_at`. A run that is already
  succeeded, failed or cancelled answers 409, unchanged. A cancelled run frees the job,
  so it can be run again.
- **Allowed status moves:** queued → running or cancelled; running → succeeded, failed or
  cancelled. A finished run never changes again.
- **Consistency:**
  - `finished_at` is set exactly when the run is succeeded, failed or cancelled;
  - a queued run has no `started_at`;
  - `exit_code` is set exactly when the run succeeded or failed, and 0 means succeeded;
  - a manual run records who triggered it, and a cron run records no one.

## Ticket 4: the worker
- A worker executes queued runs:
  - claim the run (running, with `started_at`);
  - run `command` as an argument list (**no shell**), with the repo's `code_path` as the
    working directory, under a timeout (`Settings.RunTimeout`);
  - record the result: succeeded with exit 0, or failed with the exit code.
- A timeout, or a process that can't be started, is a failure.
- A run cancelled before it was claimed is never executed.
- **Cancelling a running run stops it:** the process, and its children, are terminated,
  and the run stays cancelled with no exit code.
- `POST /worker/run-once` (super admin only) processes every run that is queued, until none
  is left, and answers 200 `{"processed": n}`.
- A background loop (a `server worker` subcommand) does the same in production.

## Ticket 5: cron scheduling
- `POST /worker/schedule-tick` (super admin only) takes `{"now": ISO datetime}`. For every
  active cron config whose `cron_expr` matches that minute, it queues a run with
  `trigger="cron"` and `triggered_by` null. It answers 200 `{"queued": n}`.
- It never queues a second run for a config in the same minute, and never while the
  config has a queued or running run.
- Inactive configs and non-cron configs are never scheduled.
- A background loop (a `server scheduler` subcommand) calls it once a minute with the real time. Missed minutes are not
  back-filled.

`POST /auth/login` takes `{email, password}` and returns `{access_token, token_type: "bearer"}` (a JWT, HS256 with `Settings.SecretKey`; `sub` = user id; it expires after 60 minutes).
A wrong password or an unknown email answers 401 `{"detail": "Incorrect email or password"}`.
An inactive user answers 403 `{"detail": "Inactive user"}`.
Every other route needs a bearer token:
no token: 401 `{"detail": "Not authenticated"}`;
a bad token: 401 `{"detail": "Could not validate credentials"}`;
rule_rows.note: a scenario step cannot send an arbitrary (bad) bearer token

rule_rows.text: an inactive user: 403 `"Inactive user"`.
rule_rows.note: no scenario can hold an inactive user's token: login refuses one and no route deactivates a user

rule_rows.text: `GET /users/me` returns `{id, email, is_super_admin, is_active}`.

`POST /users` (super admin only) creates a user from `{email, password}`. Passwords are 8 to 72 bytes (bcrypt's limit); anything else answers 422. It answers 201 with the user. A duplicate email answers 409; an invalid email answers 422.
`POST /applications` (super admin only) takes `{name}` and answers 201 `{id, name}`. A duplicate name answers 409; a name that is empty or over 100 characters answers 422.
`GET /applications` returns every application to the super admin; everyone else gets only the ones they are a member of. Ordered by id.
`GET /applications/{id}` returns the application.
`GET /applications/{id}/members` (app admin or super admin) returns `[{user_id, role}]`.

`PUT /applications/{id}/members/{user_id}` takes `{role}`. It creates the membership, or changes its role (never a second membership), and answers 200 `{user_id, role}`. An unknown user answers 404; an invalid role answers 422.
`DELETE /applications/{id}/members/{user_id}` answers 204. If there is no such membership, it answers 404.
A refused or invalid request writes nothing.
`POST /applications/{app}/jobs` (app admin or super admin) takes `{name, job_name, version, code_path, command, is_cron, cron_expr}` and answers 201 with the config.
A new config is **inactive**, and `created_by` is the caller.
**Validation** (each failure answers 422 and writes nothing):
`job_name`: `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, 1–100 characters.
`name`: 1–100 characters.
`version`: 1–50 characters.
`code_path`: relative, inside the repo, with no `..` and not absolute.
`command`: 1–1000 characters. Its executable (the first token) must be in the allowlist `Settings.ExecutableAllowlist` (`python`, `bash`, `sh`).
`is_cron` true needs a valid 5-field `cron_expr`; `is_cron` false needs `cron_expr` to be null.
`(application, job_name, version)` is unique. A duplicate answers 409. The same job_name and version in another application is fine.
`GET /applications/{app}/jobs` (any member) returns the configs ordered by id. `GET /applications/{app}/jobs/{id}` returns one config.

`POST .../jobs/{id}/activate` (app admin or super admin) makes this version active and every other version of the same job inactive. **At most one active version per job.** `POST .../jobs/{id}/deactivate` makes it inactive.
**A registered version never changes.** There is no edit route, so `PATCH` answers 405; a change means registering a new version.
A config id from another application, under this application's path, answers 404.
`POST /applications/{app}/jobs/{id}/runs` (any member, or the super admin) answers 201 with a run: `trigger="manual"`, `triggered_by` = the caller, `status="queued"`.
An inactive config answers 409 and creates no run.
**At most one queued or running run per config:** another one answers 409.

`GET /applications/{app}/jobs/{id}/runs` returns the config's runs ordered by id; `GET /applications/{app}/runs/{run_id}` returns one run. A run has: id, job_config_id, application_id, trigger, triggered_by, status, created_at, started_at, finished_at, exit_code.

`POST /applications/{app}/runs/{run_id}/cancel` (any member, or the super admin) moves a queued or running run to `cancelled` and sets `finished_at`. A run that is already succeeded, failed or cancelled answers 409, unchanged. A cancelled run frees the job, so it can be run again.
**Allowed status moves:** queued → running or cancelled; running → succeeded, failed or cancelled. A finished run never changes again.
**Consistency:**
`finished_at` is set exactly when the run is succeeded, failed or cancelled;
a queued run has no `started_at`;
`exit_code` is set exactly when the run succeeded or failed, and 0 means succeeded;
a manual run records who triggered it, and a cron run records no one.
A worker executes queued runs:
claim the run (running, with `started_at`);
run `command` as an argument list (**no shell**), with the repo's `code_path` as the working directory, under a timeout (`Settings.RunTimeout`);
record the result: succeeded with exit 0, or failed with the exit code.
A timeout, or a process that can't be started, is a failure.
A run cancelled before it was claimed is never executed.
**Cancelling a running run stops it:** the process, and its children, are terminated, and the run stays cancelled with no exit code.
rule_rows.note: the repo has no long-running fixture, so a run cannot be cancelled while its process runs

rule_rows.text: `POST /worker/run-once` (super admin only) processes every run that is queued, until none is left, and answers 200 `{"processed": n}`.
A background loop (a `server worker` subcommand) does the same in production.

`POST /worker/schedule-tick` (super admin only) takes `{"now": ISO datetime}`. For every active cron config whose `cron_expr` matches that minute, it queues a run with `trigger="cron"` and `triggered_by` null. It answers 200 `{"queued": n}`.
It never queues a second run for a config in the same minute, and never while the config has a queued or running run.
Inactive configs and non-cron configs are never scheduled.
A background loop (a `server scheduler` subcommand) calls it once a minute with the real time. Missed minutes are not back-filled.

invariants: No two users share an email.
No two applications share a name.
An application's name is not empty.
A user has at most one membership in an application.
An application has at most one config per (job_name, version).
A job (application, job_name) has at most one active version.
A config's name, job_name, version and command are not empty.
A cron config has a cron_expr; a non-cron config has none.
A config has at most one queued or running run.
finished_at is set exactly when the run succeeded, failed or was cancelled.
A queued run has no started_at.
A running, succeeded or failed run was claimed: it has a started_at.
exit_code is set exactly when the run succeeded (0) or failed (non-zero).
A manual run records who triggered it; a cron run records no one.
machines: queued -> running, cancelled; running -> succeeded, failed, cancelled (initial: queued)
services: queues cron runs once a minute (the `server scheduler` loop)

- id: Int (key)
- application_id: Int
- name: Str
- job_name: Str
- version: Str
- code_path: Str
- command: Str
- is_cron: Bool
- cron_expr: Str (nullable)
- is_active: Bool
- created_by: Int
- created_at: DateTime
- key: (application_id, job_name, version)

### JobRun (job_runs)

- id: Int (key)
- job_config_id: Int
- application_id: Int
- trigger: Str (one of manual, cron)
- triggered_by: Int (nullable)
- status: Str (one of queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled)
- created_at: DateTime
- started_at: DateTime (nullable)
- finished_at: DateTime (nullable)
- exit_code: Int (nullable)

## Invariants

- **one_account_per_email**: No two users share an email.
- **one_application_per_name**: No two applications share a name.
- **application_name_not_empty**: An application's name is not empty.
- **one_membership_per_user_and_application**: A user has at most one membership in an application.
- **unique_job_version**: An application has at most one config per (job_name, version).
- **one_active_version_per_job**: A job (application, job_name) has at most one active version.
- **job_config_fields_not_empty**: A config's name, job_name, version and command are not empty.
- **cron_expr_only_for_cron_configs**: A cron config has a cron_expr; a non-cron config has none.
- **one_live_run_per_config**: A config has at most one queued or running run.
- **finished_at_exactly_when_finished**: finished_at is set exactly when the run succeeded, failed or was cancelled.
- **queued_run_not_started**: A queued run has no started_at.
- **executed_run_has_started_at**: A running, succeeded or failed run was claimed: it has a started_at.
- **exit_code_exactly_when_ended**: exit_code is set exactly when the run succeeded (0) or failed (non-zero).
- **trigger_matches_triggered_by**: A manual run records who triggered it; a cron run records no one.

## State machines

- **JobRun.status**: queued -> running, cancelled; running -> succeeded, failed, cancelled (initial: queued)

## Background services

- **worker**: executes queued runs (the `server worker` loop)
- **scheduler**: queues cron runs once a minute (the `server scheduler` loop)
